wstep: This card describes the NCHFP recipe for mint jelly: an infusion of fresh mint made into a jelly with sugar, lemon juice and liquid pectin and processed in a boiling-water bath. [T:ACI-309,ACI-311,ACI-313]

sekcje.naglowek: Why you must not change the recipe
akapity: The FDA list gives parsley, a garden herb, a pH of about 5.70–6.00, so herbs on their own are not an acid food. [T:ACI-117]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): do not change the amounts of the acid ingredients or of the fruit and vegetables; the recipe is tested only in the proportions given. [T:ACI-265]
NCHFP warns not to reduce the sugar in traditional recipes: too little sugar prevents gelling and may allow yeasts and molds to grow. [T:SLO-001]
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml. [T:ACI-195]

For about 3 or 4 half-pint jars NCHFP uses 1 3/4 cups of mint juice (made from 1 1/2 cups of firmly packed fresh mint and 2 1/4 cups of water), 3 1/2 cups of sugar, 2 tablespoons of lemon juice and 1 pouch (3 ounces) of liquid pectin. [T:ACI-309]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use bottled lemon juice in the amount given; NCHFP notes that fresh lemon juice can vary in acidity. [T:ACI-314,SLO-039]
Sterilize the jars and prepare two-piece lids according to the manufacturer. [T:ACI-310]

NCHFP puts the empty jars right side up on the rack in a boiling-water canner and fills the canner and jars with hot (not boiling) water to 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) above the tops of the jars. [T:SLO-120]
To sterilize empty jars, NCHFP boils them for 10 minutes below 1000 ft, and above that 1 minute longer for each additional thousand feet. [T:SLO-118]
JarAtlas rule for metres: boil the jars for 10 minutes up to 300 m, and add 1 minute for every further 300 m or part of it. [T:SLO-119]
Wash the mint and crush or finely chop the leaves and stems. [T:ACI-310]
Put the mint in a saucepan, add the water and bring quickly to a boil. [T:ACI-310]
Remove from the heat, cover and let stand for 10 minutes. [T:ACI-310]
Strain out the mint and discard it. [T:ACI-310]
Measure 1 3/4 cups of mint juice into a large saucepot and stir in the sugar and lemon juice. [T:ACI-311]
Over high heat, stirring constantly, bring to a full boil that cannot be stirred down. [T:ACI-311]
Add the liquid pectin, bring back to a full rolling boil and boil hard for 1 minute. [T:ACI-311]
Remove from the heat and quickly skim off the foam. [T:ACI-311]
Just before filling, remove and drain the hot sterilized jars one at a time. [T:SLO-120]
Pour the hot jelly immediately into hot, sterile jars, leaving 1/4 inch (about 0.6 cm) of headspace. [T:ACI-312]
Wipe the jar rims with a damp clean paper towel, put on two-piece metal lids and process in a boiling-water canner. [T:ACI-312]
At 0–1000 ft (up to 300 m) process half-pint and pint jars for 5 minutes. [T:ACI-313,ACI-176]
Above 1000 ft the food may spoil if the time is not increased. [T:ACI-015]
At 1001–6000 ft (above 300 m up to 1800 m) process them for 10 minutes. [T:ACI-322,ACI-176]
Above 6000 ft (above 1800 m) process them for 15 minutes. [T:ACI-323,ACI-176]
The card converts feet to metres and rounds the limits down, towards the longer time: 1000 ft becomes 300 m and 6000 ft becomes 1800 m. [T:ACI-176]
Shortening the time or cooling jars in cold water can also lead to spoilage. [T:ACI-015]
The NCHFP table gives times only for half-pint and pint jars. [T:ACI-313]
JarAtlas rule (NCHFP does not test metric jars): a pint holds about 473 ml, so a 0.5 l jar has no tested time in this recipe; use jars of up to 473 ml. [T:ACI-179,ACI-174]
Keep opened jelly in the refrigerator at 40 °F (about 4 °C) or lower. [T:SLO-018]
Discard jelly with mold on it; USDA and microbiologists advise against scooping out the mold and eating the rest. [T:SLO-012]
